fact_en:
Why is the traditional salakot hat so cool and comfy?

It's woven from solid, lightweight rattan! This clever design allows gas, like air, to flow through easily.
fact_bis:
Nganong komportable kaayo magsuot og tradisyonal nga salakot?

Hiniusa kini gikan sa lig-on pero gaan nga rattan! Mao nga dali moagi ang gas o hangin sulod.
evidence: Last word "Salako" is cut off; the card itself contains "Salakot".

fact_en: Cooking milkfish bones in vinegar causes a chemical change that dissolves the solid calcium into a liquid solution!
fact_bis: Kung lutuon ang bukog sa bangus gamit ang suka, mo-occur ang chemical change nga mo-dissolve sa solid nga calcium ngadto sa liquid solution!
evidence: Cebuano "buto" means an explosion/blast (and is crude slang in some areas), not bone — the card's own body correctly says "bukog", so the headline reads "Explosion Milkfish Vinegar Calcium" to a Cebuano child.

fact_en:
What are our bones made of?

Bones are solid organs made mostly of a rigid matrix of calcium phosphate minerals and flexible collagen proteins!
fact_bis:
Unsay gihimo sa atong mga bukog?

Ang mga bukog kay solid organs nga gibuhat sa rigid matrix sa calcium phosphate minerals ug flexible collagen proteins!
evidence: Title "Buto Calcium Collagen" uses the Tagalog word for bone; in Cebuano "buto" = blast/explosion while the card itself uses "bukog" throughout.

fact_en: Friction makes real-world motion tricky, but Newton's laws still hold! We just count friction as one more force in the net force.
fact_bis: Makalibog ang friction sa tinuod nga kalibutan, pero molihok gihapon ang mga balaod ni Newton! I-dugang lang nato ang friction sa net force.
evidence: "Bala" is a bullet, not a law — the body correctly uses "balaod ni Newton", so "Newton Bala uban Friction" reads as "Newton Bullet with Friction".

fact_en: When two forces push in the same direction, their strengths add together to make a larger force!
fact_bis: Kung ang duha ka pwersa motukmod sa samang direksyon, magdugtong ang ilang kusog aron makahimo og mas dako nga pwersa!
evidence: Title ends on a bare particle with its head noun missing.

fact_en: By the law of conservation of energy, energy cannot be created or destroyed. It only changes form while the total amount stays the same!
fact_bis: Sumala sa balaod sa conservation of energy, dili mahimo o mawala ang enerhiya. Mausab lang kini og porma samtang magpabilin nga pareho ang kinatibuk-an!
evidence: "Conservation sa Energy Bala" names a bullet rather than the law ("balaod") the card's own body uses.

fact_en: Soft things like pillows and curtains soak up sound instead of bouncing it! Shouting into a pillow makes a muffled sound, which is why recording studios use soft walls to trap sound.
fact_bis: Ang humok nga butang sama sa unlan ug kurtina mosuyop sa tingog! Mao nga hinay ang singgit sa unlan, ug nagagamit og humok nga bongbong ang recording studio aron mapugngan ang tingog.
evidence: "Lumot" is moss/algae in Cebuano, not soft — the card is about soft materials (body: "humok") absorbing sound, so the headline introduces moss that appears nowhere in the card.

fact_en: A fan doesn't cool the air! It just blows air across your skin so your sweat evaporates faster, carrying heat away to make you feel cooler.
fact_bis: Ang bentilador dili gyud mopabugnaw sa hangin! Gihuyop lang niini ang hangin sa panit aron mas paspas mosingaw ang singot, nga modala sa init palayo aron mabugnaw ta.
evidence: "Bahu" means stink/odour, not sweat — the card is about sweat ("singot" in the body) evaporating, and it never mentions smell, so the headline points at the wrong mechanism.

fact_en:
How does a spring balance measure weight?

A heavier object stretches the spring inside it more! This stretching is how it measures weight.
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagsukod sa kabug-aton sa spring balance?

Ang mas bug-at nga butang mas mobira sa tinggol sa sulod niini! Mao ni kini nga nagsukod sa kabug-aton.
evidence: A spring balance's spring is a metal coil (body: "tinggol"), but "bukal" in Cebuano is boiling/a water source, so "Timbangan sa Bukal" names a completely different kind of spring.

fact_en:
Who created the three laws of motion?

The three laws of motion were made by the English scientist Isaac Newton!
fact_bis:
Kinsa ang naghimo sa tulo ka balaod sa paglihok?

Ang tulo ka balaod sa paglihok gihimo sa English nga siyentipiko nga si Isaac Newton!
terms: sino gumawa ng batas ng galaw
kinsa naghimo sa balaod sa lihok
evidence: "Si Isaac Newton Tulo Bala" reads as "three bullets"; the card is about the three laws of motion, which the body correctly calls "balaod".

fact_en:
When and where did Isaac Newton publish his laws of motion?

He published them in the year 1687 in his book called the Principia!
fact_bis:
Kanus-a ug asa gipatik ni Isaac Newton ang iyang mga balaod sa paglihok?

Gipatik niya kini niadtong tuig 1687 sa iyang libro nga gitawag og Principia!
evidence: "1687 Principia Bala Kalihukan" uses "bala" (bullet) where the card and its body mean "balaod sa paglihok" (laws of motion).

fact_en:
Why do ball bearings make skateboard wheels spin faster?

They convert sliding friction into rolling friction, which reduces heat and lets the wheel spin faster!
fact_bis:
Nganong mas paspas moikot ang ligid sa skateboard kung naay ball bearings?

Ang ball bearings nag-convert sa sliding friction ngadto sa rolling friction, nga makapamenos sa kainit ug makapaspas sa pag-ikot!
evidence: Last word "Frictio" is cut off; the card itself contains "Friction".
